journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers, in their house in Blackrose, has need of one who will help a woman held by an Owing on the estate north of the town. I'm to find Never-Sold at the estate's landing and do what she asks.
directions: From Blackrose take the swamp road north out of the town; the estate's landing is a short walk on, on the channel side, with a work shed and boats at the water. The chest is inside the shed on the left.

journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me to free Rows-For-Another, who took a boat from an estate north of Blackrose on four months' work eleven years ago. She will not wait on the book of Hulm-Tei, the estate's steward. At night two estate men walk the estate landing north of Blackrose, and the channel runs from the landing out of the estate's reach; she cannot drown in it. I'm to come back after dark and take her down the channel to where it leaves the estate.
directions: The channel runs past the landing's boats north-east, away from the road; where it leaves the estate it passes under a fallen trunk.

journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me to free Rows-For-Another, who took a boat from an estate north of Blackrose on four months' work eleven years ago. I took the steward's debt book from the work shed, and Never-Sold put it before Hulm-Tei and named him a slaver to his face. By his own true lines the buy-out came down to what Rows-For-Another first owed, and Never-Sold paid it. She walks off the swamp road free, without her boat.

Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me to free Rows-For-Another, who took a boat from an estate north of Blackrose on four months' work eleven years ago. She would not wait on the steward's book. After dark I took her past the two estate men and down the channel until it left the estate. She is free and gone, and can never go back to the swamp road.

Never-Sold told me the cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose's edge are burning. The Rose is the old Imperial prison a day's march on, and the heirs, born of the prisoners once held there, keep it and this post; three they hold are inside, Rows-For-Another's mother among them. The heirs' gate-keepers will not go in. I'm to get through the stockade gate at the outer post, by talking Third-Born Tsaxi round or slipping past, and go down into the cells.
directions: The outer post is a short walk south-west of the Chainbreakers' house, where the stockade of stakes stands round a low door, under BM&V's 'Black Rose Jail' marker.

journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me into the burning cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose's edge. Three the heirs hold are inside, each reached its own way. Says-It-Plain is behind a lock; Hides-In-Reeds is up a collapsed way; Keeps-The-Old-Count is in the flooded cell. When the first comes away with me, the fire takes the other two. I'm to reach one of them, tell them to come with me, and bring them out through the cells' door.
directions: From the door the passage forks three ways in the smoke; the locked cell is straight on, the collapsed way climbs on the left, and the flooded cell is down the steps on the right. The way out is back up the passage to the cells' door.

journal_text: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me into the burning cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose, where the heirs held three. I brought Says-It-Plain out; the other two died in the fire. He walked free from the jail door, to speak their names to Never-Sold.

Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me into the burning cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose, where the heirs held three. I brought Hides-In-Reeds out; the other two died in the fire. She does not deny her killing. She walked free from the jail door, to speak their names to Never-Sold.

Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me into the burning cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose, where the heirs held three. I brought Keeps-The-Old-Count, Rows-For-Another's mother, out; the other two died in the fire. She walked free from the jail door, to speak their names to Never-Sold.

Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers sent me into the burning cells under the Rose's outer post at Blackrose, where the heirs held three. Nobody came out. Never-Sold at the Chainbreakers' house keeps the three names herself.

On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years, refused to let Heavy-Rope's crew end their last season early. The crew know me as the Chainbreakers'. I'm to hear Ussa-Rekh and Heavy-Rope on the dock and take one side.
directions: Soulrest's open dock is the long dock on the town's water, where the crews wait for hire; Ussa-Rekh keeps his chest beside him on the planks.

journal_text: I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew on Soulrest's open dock. Ussa-Rekh keeps their carved tokens in the chest beside him on the dock, and he promised that a crew who break their tokens before him are done with him. I'm to take the tokens from the chest and give them to Heavy-Rope.
directions: Ussa-Rekh's chest stands on the planks beside him, on a low lock.

journal_text: I stood with Ussa-Rekh on Soulrest's open dock. Heavy-Rope will not take the refusal from a stranger's mouth. I'm to talk him into taking it, or pay his crew to take it.
directions: Heavy-Rope waits at the middle of the dock, among his crew.

journal_text: On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and hires out the crews he freed, refused to let Heavy-Rope's crew end their last season early. I stood with the crew: I took their tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest and gave them to Heavy-Rope, and the crew broke them before him. They are done with him a season early, and he will hire neither of them again.

On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and hires out the crews he freed, refused to let Heavy-Rope's crew end their last season early. I stood with Ussa-Rekh and talked Heavy-Rope into taking the refusal. The crew will work their last season under him.

On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and hires out the crews he freed, refused to let Heavy-Rope's crew end their last season early. I stood with Ussa-Rekh and paid Heavy-Rope's crew 50 gold to take the refusal. The crew will work their last season under him.

On Soulrest's open dock the broker Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and hires out the crews he freed, refused to let Heavy-Rope's crew end their last season early. One of them is dead, and the matter died with him.

I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford in the morning, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me the landing began charging walkers at the ford. The landing worked this ford before the well was dug. The landing will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut before the rains. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft. In the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft; in the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and have the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo before the rains: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing would take half a charge for water it never draws. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it. Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.
directions: Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk; Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing has rammed its clay in behind the cracked lining before the rains. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut at night. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.
The rains came to Claywater Station before I made terms between Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo. The well is still cracked. Travellers still pay at both banks or wade below the ford at night.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing will make no terms with Livia Varinius and the station while it mourns. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to get into the pool, with her leave or without it at night.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I have gone into the pool under the Hist at Greenspring. I'm to search the spring's throat between the roots, where the water comes up.

A dead man lies staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring, his wrists tied with rope, the stake left blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him, before the killer leaves.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal sleeps in the lodge and goes to the stone lip after the lamps are out.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro has had the body raised and given to the Hist, and the root-herald holds Reeh-Shaal for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro has had the courier's body raised from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her go. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The village has closed ranks against me, and Reeh-Shaal has taken the boat.
Reeh-Shaal has left Greenspring on the Helstrom boat. Whoever killed the courier in the spring has gone, and the guests are still sick.
A rafter at Helstrom's landing, Okan-Zish, wants the beast under the crew's plank walk killed. I'm to find its lair in the shallows under the walk and kill it, or shoot or burn it from the planks.
directions: Okan-Zish stands north along the shore from the ship's door, by the houses where a levy soldier stands. The crew's plank walk runs along the shore there; the lair is in the shallows under it, with the crew's bait bucket.

journal_text: The beast is dead. In its lair in the shallows under the plank walk lies the landing crew's bait bucket, offal in it: the crew's offal drew the beast that has kept traders off the river and off the boat captain's boat. I'm to take the bucket to the boat captain, who stands at Helstrom's north edge west of the levy's gate, or put it to Wuleen-Taza and take the crew's price to keep quiet.
directions: Wuleen-Taza stands by the crew's houses with the levy soldier. The boat captain stands at Helstrom's north edge, west of the levy's gate.

journal_text: I showed the boat captain the crew's bait bucket. She paid me for what it showed her, and the crew have lost their trade on the river to her.
Wuleen-Taza paid me to keep the bait to myself. The crew keep their trade, and the boat captain still thinks the river took her customers.
The boat captain is dead. There is no one left on the river for the crew's bait to cheat.
A woman, Haj-Wan, waits inside Helstrom's basin gate, beside the levy warden, for her kin Sei-Wan, who walked out alone into the basin. He went east through the shallows. I'm to find him.
directions: Haj-Wan waits inside the gate, beside the levy warden. Out of the gate, the shallows run east; Sei-Wan is pinned among the roots there, and the viper lies by him.

journal_text: The viper that kept Sei-Wan pinned among the roots in the basin is dead. I can go back west to Helstrom's basin gate without a word to him and let him walk home alone, or talk to him and bring him back myself.
directions: Sei-Wan is among the roots; the gate is back west through the shallows.

journal_text: I am back at Helstrom's basin gate, and I left Sei-Wan without a word. He walks home alone, and his walk-out is his own.
I talked Sei-Wan into coming home. He knows he was followed, and he will not count the walk-out as his own or look at me.
Sei-Wan is dead in the basin. His walk-out ended there, and Haj-Wan waits at the gate for no one.

I came to in the hold of a broker's barge at Lilmoth's dock, among an Owing gang. Wuleen-Sei, the overseer, is reading the roll aloud, each name, the months owed and the months added for food, and my line is blank. I'm to answer her when she reaches it, then follow Wuleen-Sei up the plank, past Buys-The-Months, the broker on the pier, and north and west along the shore path to the families' camp at the edge of Hereguard Plantation, to the camp's fire.
directions: The hold is the barge's one room below the deck; its door leads up to the plank and the pier of Lilmoth's dock. From the plank at Lilmoth's dock the shore path runs north and west along the water, past the first of the rice dikes; the camp is the cluster of huts on the reed bank at the paddy edge, where the path meets the reeds. The fire is in the middle of the camp; the hatching shed stands beside the cutting at the camp's far end.

journal_text: As Wuleen-Sei read the roll at the camp's fire, in sight of the families' Hist cutting and the shed that holds their clutch, naming Sal-Sei, keeper of the clutch, and Deesh-Duun aloud, a tall Argonian woman with a knotted cord at her wrist came in off the water with two of her people, killed Mee-Tuja, the quiet man who walked with us, at the fire, took his satchel and looked at me, and left. In the struggle his strap with a brass tag was torn off and fell through the burnt boards into the deep water. The roll went into the fire. Her people are at the cutting and the huts are burning. Sal-Sei is at the shed and Deesh-Duun is hiding from the blades in the huts. I'm to reach one of them; I cannot reach both.
directions: The shed is at the camp's far end beside the cutting; the cell's two cutters stand between the fire and the shed. The burning huts stand over the deep water under the plank boards and are entered only from the water.

journal_text: I ran for the hatching shed at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge. Two of the woman's people have cut the roots that tie the cutting to the clutch, and Sal-Sei is on the ground beside the eggs. Behind me the huts have fallen in where Deesh-Duun was. I'm to drive the cutters off, or hide in the reeds until they leave, and get Sal-Sei out through the reeds to the shore.
directions: From the shed the reeds run south to the shore below the camp, the way the families fish at night; keep the burning huts on the left hand.

journal_text: I went into the burning huts at the camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge and pulled Deesh-Duun out through the deep water under the plank boards. She saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. From the water I can hear the cutters on the plank boards over us, walking from the shed to the water's edge where they came in, and Sal-Sei has not come out. I'm to bring Deesh-Duun south under the plank boards to the shore below the camp, keeping out of the cutters' sight until they are gone, or kill them first.
directions: The shore is south of the huts; keep under the plank boards and the burning end of the camp stays on the left hand.

journal_text: I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Sal-Sei, the clutch-keeper. The eggs under the cut roots are dead and the cutting has withdrawn. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe, and nobody can say what I do not.

I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge with Deesh-Duun, who saw the woman with the knotted cord as closely as I did. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.
I got out of the burning camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge alone. Sal-Sei and Deesh-Duun are dead. The roll burned in the fire, so nobody can say what I owe.

The camp on Hereguard Plantation's paddy edge is a ruin and I came out of the fire burnt. Two strangers, who say a friend of the courier's sent them, are taking off the hurt. Sap the cutters spilled lies on the shed floor, and the courier Mee-Tuja's brass tag fell through the burnt plank boards at the fire into the deep water. I'm to taste the sap, take a phial of it or dive for the tag in the families' sunk fish-trap and pick the trap's lock, and then tell the stranger on the shore I am ready to go.
directions: The shed stands beside the withdrawn cutting at the camp's far end. The burnt plank boards lie at the camp's fire over the deep water; the courier's strap and tag lie in the families' locked fish-trap on the bottom straight below them, one breath down; lockpicks lie loose on the boards beside the fire.

journal_text: The strangers took the hurt to a house in Lilmoth that a fish-trader, Salts-The-Catch, keeps. In the back room, behind a screen, a woman who calls herself Nesh-Deeka sits by the mats, and Ties-The-Loose-Plank lies on one of them. Nesh-Deeka is of the Veiled Reed. The roll burnt at the camp, so nobody can show what I owe or that I was on it, and almost no one knows my face. I'm to tell her what I saw, and get Ties to tell it too, then answer her offer of the oath.
directions: The house has no mark; the back room is past the front room's table, behind the screen, the mats beside it. The street door opens from inside; the camp is the shore path north and west of the dock.

journal_text: I lay down on the mats in the house in Lilmoth with the camp's sap still on my tongue, and dreamed. I stood in fog among a ring of trees whose roots climbed up and up, and at the top was a gap like a door that nobody has built. A dry voice spoke that I could not place. The dream walked me to the door.
directions: The roots of the ring rise from the fog to the door-gap at the top; the dream walks you there.

journal_text: The dream led me to the door, and I woke in the house in Lilmoth. I have taken the Veiled Reed's oath: Nesh-Deeka says no one will come asking what I owe, the house's door is open to me, and she put the first of a stipend in my hand.
The dream led me to the door, and I woke in the house in Lilmoth. I have taken no oath. The house's door is not mine, but the Reed will send for me when it has work, and pay for it.

The Reed sent me east of Lilmoth to Low-Reed Village, where the Hist has turned its face. The root-herald, on the platform at the Hist's foot, does not like strangers from Lilmoth. I'm to talk her round, or bring her food, for leave to see the tree.
directions: The village lies east of Lilmoth along the reed paths, its jetty on the west side; the root-herald keeps the platform at the Hist's foot.

journal_text: The tending-ground at Low-Reed Village is closed, the Hist dark and its leaves shut, and the uxith is dark, as it was at the camp. The village says the leeches did it. I'm to go down into the water under the stilts, to the tree's lowest root, and see for myself.
directions: The roots run down from the tending-ground into the water under the stilts; the cut root is the lowest.

journal_text: A root of the Hist was cut at the ring and sealed with black gum, and the leeches only came to the weeping sap. Pays-Late, the tree-minder, whom the village blames, goes down to wash it after dark. I'm to watch him there unseen at night, or ask the egg-tender at the uxith by day, and find out who cut it.
directions: Pays-Late goes down to the cut root after dark; the egg-tender keeps the uxith by day.

journal_text: A root of Low-Reed Village's Hist was cut and its sap drawn off. I'm to swim the leech water north of the village, follow the bent reeds to the camp on the dry rise, take the jars of the Hist's sap, and pour them back at the cut root under the stilts.
directions: The leech water lies north of the village where the reeds open; past it the bent reed stems lead to a dry rise past the last stilt house. The cut root is under the stilts.

journal_text: I poured the jars back at the cut root and left Pays-Late's knife with them. The village knows now that it was strangers' work and not his keeping. The Hist's light is coming back, low and slow. The village has taken me in.
The cell cut a Hist's root at Low-Reed Village for its sap, and I saw the cut. I'm to take what I found back to Nesh-Deeka at the fish-trader's house in Lilmoth, which is the Reed's.
directions: The Reed's house is the fish-trader's, Salts-The-Catch's, on the stilts of Lilmoth's channel; its back room is behind the screen.

journal_text: The Reed wants the tree-minders and Nisswo of Helstrom to hear what a cut Hist looks like, from someone the Reed can deny; it sends no escort. I'm to take the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop: one of its doors opens on Helstrom's river landing. From the landing I'm to follow the marsh way north-east, root and shallows, past the gate at the city's edge to the grove behind the Hall of the Scalded Throne.
directions: The coast ship lies at Lilmoth's stop on the east side. Go in by its door at the stop (0AA837, the pair of 0AA664) and through the ship to the door that opens on the river landing (23D496, the pair of 0830A8 on the landing, where BM&V's map marker reads Helstrom); that door is found by its place in the ship, measured at build. The inner door joins the ship's two sections; where it stands is measured at build. From the landing the way runs inland, root and shallows; at its far bend, where it turns toward the city, two giant wasps keep the root over the Heart-Mud. Past the bend the way runs to the gate soldier at the city's edge. The grove is behind the Hall of the Scalded Throne, by the first street.

journal_text: Behind the hall Kaska-Meen keeps her watch in the grove, and at the root's foot a Nisswo, Ei-Tuja, argues with her over what a silent Hist means. Neither has seen a cut root. I saw one. I'm to tell one of them that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. The Hall of the Scalded Throne, by the first street on the left inside the gate, holds a plain seat of root and reed, with no dais, swept with a broom, and the city sells in the room before it.
directions: The Hall of the Scalded Throne is the low-roofed house by the first street, on the left as the way comes in from the gate; its inner room holds the seat and its outer room the merchants. The grove is the stand of root behind the hall: Ei-Tuja stands at the root's foot and Kaska-Meen sits at her watch by the young Hist.

journal_text: In the grove I told Kaska-Meen what I saw at Low-Reed Village: that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. She heard me out and will carry it to the interior's tree-minders. The Reed is not named in Helstrom.

At the root's foot I told Ei-Tuja what I saw at Low-Reed Village: that a Hist gone silent and a Hist cut at the root are two things, and the clutch died of the cut. He gave his reading freely, as the Nisswo do, and will carry it to the villages he preaches in. The Reed is not named in Helstrom.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The village blames the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. Ixo-Vaal has called the office-holders to the Hist. I'm to put what I found before them and argue for a cure, and for whether the founders are named.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and named the deed at the Hist. The tree should mend, and Greenspring now owes the people of the dead grove an answer.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and agreed to say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
Greenspring chose to reopen the founders' cut downstream. Their Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.

Tilts-The-Jug, inside the house on Soulrest's dock, keeps the Chapter's desk at Soulrest and wants to see how I work. Keeps-What-Floats, a dock thief, took a necklace of polished blue jaspers from another thief, and it must come back with no harm done to him. I'm to follow him on the dock until he goes to his bed for the night, or get out of Sits-By-The-Water, who drinks with him, where he sleeps.
directions: He walks the dock west of the house by day, and in the evening he drinks at the bench by the water with Sits-By-The-Water; where he sleeps is learnt by following him or from her.

journal_text: Keeps-What-Floats, who took the necklace of blue jaspers, keeps it on him on the dock by day, at the bench by the water in the evening, and on his bedroll north-west of the house at night. I'm to get the necklace back without hurting him, by lifting it off him by day or while he sleeps, or by talking him out of it, and bring it to Tilts-The-Jug inside Soulrest's house.
directions: By day he is on the dock west of the house; in the evening he drinks at the bench by the water, and at night he sleeps on his bedroll north-west of the house. Tilts-The-Jug is inside the house, behind its one open door.

journal_text: I brought the necklace of blue jaspers back to Tilts-The-Jug at Soulrest, and Keeps-What-Floats came to no harm. She paid me and gave me three lockpicks. The Chapter's way down is a locked trapdoor two squares north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, open the trapdoor, go down to the Chapter and speak to whoever waits below.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock (039827); inside the ship, the other door (0AA837) comes out at Lilmoth Dock (0AA664), on Lilmoth's east side. Walk west to the Lilmoth Hist; Pusbottom lies past it by the canals, and the trapdoor (16BF7F) is in the ground two squares north of Pusbottom. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the Chapter's inner room, past the foot of the trapdoor's ladder.

journal_text: I brought the necklace of blue jaspers back to Tilts-The-Jug at Soulrest, but Keeps-What-Floats is dead. She paid me nothing, and said the Chapter wanted the necklace without a body, but she gave me three lockpicks and sent me on. The Chapter's way down is a locked trapdoor two squares north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. I'm to take the coast ship from Soulrest's dock to Lilmoth, open the trapdoor, go down to the Chapter and speak to whoever waits below.
directions: The coast ship's door is on Soulrest's dock (039827); inside the ship, the other door (0AA837) comes out at Lilmoth Dock (0AA664), on Lilmoth's east side. Walk west to the Lilmoth Hist; Pusbottom lies past it by the canals, and the trapdoor (16BF7F) is in the ground two squares north of Pusbottom. Below, Bent-Spine keeps to the Chapter's inner room, past the foot of the trapdoor's ladder.

journal_text: I got the necklace of blue jaspers back from Keeps-What-Floats at Soulrest without hurting him, and Tilts-The-Jug paid me. I opened the trapdoor north of Pusbottom with my own hand and went down to the Chapter, and Bent-Spine took me in as a Lookout.

I got the necklace of blue jaspers back at Soulrest, but Keeps-What-Floats died for it, and Tilts-The-Jug paid me nothing. I opened the trapdoor north of Pusbottom with my own hand and went down to the Chapter, and Bent-Spine took me in as a Lookout.

I'm in the Night-Reed Chapter now, under Pusbottom in Lilmoth. Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, wants the lockbox of a merchant whose stilt house fell into the deep water two squares north of Pusbottom, by the Chapter's trapdoor; it lies locked on the floor beside the house, and ripper eels hunt the water. Three clients on the bank want it. I'm to talk to each of them, Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel, and get out of each what they claim the box holds for them.
directions: Climb the trapdoor's ladder out of the Chapter; the fallen house lies in the deep water two squares north of Pusbottom by the trapdoor, and the three clients wait on its south bank.

journal_text: Neeta-Haj says the bone figurine in the lockbox was carved for her clutch, Okan-Tei that the charm was only pledged and never sold, and Dar-Zeel that the beads are old family work. The box lies locked on the floor of the deep water north of Pusbottom beside the fallen stilt house, and ripper eels hunt the water. I'm to swim down to it, slip past the eels, pick its lock and take the figurine, the charm and the beads, then settle it on the bank, by handing all three things to one client or by selling each client the thing they claimed.
directions: The fallen house lies on its side on the floor of the deep water below the bank; the lockbox is in the open beside it. The three clients wait on the bank above.

journal_text: I brought up the lockbox's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom, past the ripper eels, and gave all three to one of the clients on the bank, who paid me for them. The other two will not forget it.

I brought up the lockbox's figurine, charm and beads from the deep water north of Pusbottom, past the ripper eels, and sold each client the thing they claimed. Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei and Dar-Zeel paid, and none of them will greet me kindly again.
With one of Neeta-Haj, Okan-Tei or Dar-Zeel dead before I had settled with them, the lockbox's pledges cannot be settled, and the job for Bent-Spine has come to nothing.
